alloy.preparation: As-cast Mo0, nominal Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.5Mo0. Raw Co, Cr, Ti, Fe and Ni granules of purity above 99 wt%; induction melted at 1600 °C after argon purging. Co, Fe and Ni first melted, followed by Ti and Cr as described in the shared sequence; no FeMo addition for Mo0. Poured into a shell mold preheated at 1100 °C; ingots 8 × 7 × 14 cm. Electric-arc-line cut into 3 mm thick, 8 mm diameter cylinders; cold mounted in epoxy with 0.5 cm² exposed. Ground through 240–600-grit SiC and cleaned with acetone and distilled water.
alloy.microstructure: Simple FCC solid-solution structure; dendritic as-cast microstructure with Ni/Ti-rich interdendrites and Fe/Cr-rich dendrites. Cr/Mo-rich sigma reflections belong to higher-Mo alloys, not Mo0.

test_solution.preparation: Deaerated by bubbling purified nitrogen before and throughout electrochemical testing, under atmospheric pressure; duration and pH not stated.
test_solution.solvent: Water (source explicitly calls these aqueous environments)

test_method.procedure_description: Three-electrode cell: specimen working, Ag/AgCl in 3 M KCl reference and Pt-sheet counter; Autolab PGSTAT30. OCP recorded for 15 min, then cathodically polarized at −192 mV SHE for 5 min to reduce surface films. Cyclic scan begins at −0.5 V, moves anodically to 1.5 V versus OCP, then reverses to the starting potential as reported. Results are reported on SHE scale. Figure 5(a) shows positive hysteresis and the Mo-free alloy is identified as pitting susceptible.
test_method.pitting_criterion: Eb is the potential where current density suddenly increases; positive hysteresis establishes pitting in Mo0. New pits initiate above Eb, distinguished from the lower Eprot and Erp.

experiments.result_note: Reported breakdown potential associated with pitting in the Mo-free specimen. The lower Eprot and Erp are separate protection/repassivation quantities, not duplicate pitting potentials. Table 1 supplies reported bulk wt.% chemistry; nominal mole ratios and phase-specific EDS are not converted into bulk composition. The 3 M KCl belongs to the reference electrode, not the test electrolyte.
